elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: The inserted warranty covers only conformance ("its servicing and other services under this Agreement will conform to this Agreement and the Servicing Procedures"); the retained Section 3.2(a) "reasonable care ... degree of skill and attention" is a servicing covenant, not an express professional-and-workmanlike warranty. To meet this element the drafter must add an express warranty that the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "any software and receivables systems it provides or makes available to the Issuer under this Agreement will conform in all material respects to their documentation."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Inserted period is "for 90 days after delivery"; the 12-month preferred duration is only floated in the margin comment ("We can discuss the preferred 12-month software period"), not in operative language.
Inserted services period is "for 30 days after performance", short of the preferred 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "the Servicer will, at the Issuer's option, repair or replace the non-conforming software, system or services".
Inserted: "or refund the Servicing Fee paid for them."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 6.1(a)(ix): "It has complied with all Laws applicable to the servicing of the Receivables" (subject to a Material Adverse Effect qualifier and expressed as a point-in-time representation, which is a rationale-level note rather than an absence).

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code, virus or disabling-device warranty appears anywhere in the cited or inserted language.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "for 90 days after delivery, any software and receivables systems it provides or makes available to the Issuer under this Agreement will conform in all material respects to their documentation" — an express software-to-documentation warranty at exactly the 90-day floor.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "for 30 days after performance, its servicing and other services under this Agreement will conform to this Agreement and the Servicing Procedures."

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "the Servicer will, at the Issuer's option, repair or replace the non-conforming software, system or services".
Inserted: "or refund the Servicing Fee paid for them" — a fee-refund remedy tied to the non-conforming item.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the single inserted "Performance Warranty" paragraph supplies a 90-day software-to-documentation warranty, a 30-day services warranty, and repair/replacement or refund remedies, so the deviation finding and the fallback target are correctly matched.

Preferred level fails on four elements: the software period is 90 days rather than 12 months, the services period is 30 days rather than 90 days, there is no professional-and-workmanlike warranty (Section 3.2(a) is a servicing covenant, not a warranty), and there is no no-malicious-code warranty.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion for a missing clause, no deletion or paraphrase of existing text, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or extra damages language, and no procedure beyond the remedy itself. Electing party ("at the Issuer's option") is inherent to the remedy formulation rather than an added requirement, though it departs from the model language's Vendor-option formulation and may be a negotiation point.

Intent is preserved: Section 3.3(g)'s sole-remedy language is expressly limited to Sections 3.2(b), (c) and (d), so the new remedy is not swallowed and no retained sentence contradicts it; the Section 6.1(a) compliance representations and the acquisition-of-Receivables machinery survive intact. "Servicing Fee" and "Issuer" are defined terms, so no dangling reference is created.

If the drafter wants the preferred position, the operative repairs are: change "90 days" to twelve (12) months for software, "30 days" to ninety (90) days for services, add an express professional-and-workmanlike performance warranty, and add a no-malicious-code warranty — the margin comment's offer to discuss 12 months does not itself meet any element.
